title: Which One? N1 Look-alikes (2)
description: ずくめ vs まみれ, いまだに vs もはや, かたわら vs がてら, てっきり vs 案の定.

points.title: ずくめ vs まみれ
points.summary: ずくめ = nothing but (things, colours, often good). まみれ = smeared all over with (dirt, sweat, blood).
points.body:
- いいこと**ずくめ** / 黒**ずくめ**.
- 泥**まみれ** / 血**まみれ**.
examples: {血|ち}まみれになって{倒|たお}れていた。
He lay there covered in blood.

points.title: いまだに vs もはや
points.summary: いまだに = still (it hasn't changed). もはや = already, no longer (it has changed).
points.body:
- **いまだに**返事を待っている.
- **もはや**間に合わない.
examples: {締|し}め{切|き}りは{昨日|きのう}だった。もはや{間|ま}に{合|あ}わない。
The deadline was yesterday. It's too late now.

points.title: かたわら vs がてら
points.summary: かたわら = alongside a long-term main activity (job, studies). がてら = while out doing something (one occasion).
points.body:
- 本業の**かたわら**カフェを経営する.
- 買い物**がてら**散歩した.
examples: {本業|ほんぎょう}のかたわら、{週末|しゅうまつ}はカフェを{経営|けいえい}している。
Alongside his main job, he runs a café at weekends.

points.title: てっきり vs 案の定
points.summary: てっきり = I was sure — and I was wrong. 案の定 = just as I feared — and I was right.
points.body:
- **てっきり**晴れると思っていた (but it rained).
- **案の定**渋滞に巻き込まれた (as feared).
examples: {心配|しんぱい}していたとおり、{案|あん}の{定|じょう}{渋滞|じゅうたい}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれた。
Just as I'd feared, we got stuck in traffic.

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}いいこと（　）で、{本当|ほんとう}に{幸|しあわ}せだ。
notes: まみれ is for dirt, sweat, blood.
questions.translation: Every day is full of good things — I'm really happy.

questions.prompt: {男|おとこ}は{血|ち}（　）になって{倒|たお}れていた。
questions.translation: The man lay there covered in blood.

questions.prompt: {十年|じゅうねん}{経|た}った{今|いま}も、{彼女|かのじょ}は（　）{彼|かれ}の{返事|へんじ}を{待|ま}っている。
notes: もはや means things have changed — she's still waiting.
questions.translation: Even now, ten years on, she's still waiting for his reply.

questions.prompt: {締|し}め{切|き}りは{昨日|きのう}だった。（　）{間|ま}に{合|あ}わない。
notes: いまだに = 'still' — doesn't fit 'too late now'.
questions.translation: The deadline was yesterday. It's too late now.

questions.prompt: {本業|ほんぎょう}の（　）、{週末|しゅうまつ}はカフェを{経営|けいえい}している。
notes: かたがた is for formal visits.
がてら is for one outing, not a long-term job.
questions.translation: Alongside his main job, he runs a café at weekends.

questions.prompt: {買|か}い{物|もの}（　）、{近|ちか}くの{公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}した。
notes: かたわら is for long-term activities.
かたがた is formal (お礼かたがた).
questions.translation: While out shopping, I took a walk in the nearby park.

questions.prompt: （　）{晴|は}れると{思|おも}っていたのに、{雨|あめ}だった。
notes: 案の定 = the fear came true — but here the expectation was wrong.
questions.translation: I was sure it would be sunny, but it rained.

questions.prompt: {心配|しんぱい}していたとおり、（　）{渋滞|じゅうたい}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれた。
notes: てっきり needs と思う and a wrong belief.
questions.translation: Just as I'd feared, we got stuck in traffic.
